h1: The 5 Best Fire TVs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Fire TVs of 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 Fire TV televisions from 24 to 85 inches compared on resolution, Alexa voice control, screen size and the room each suits.
summary: The Insignia 50 inch F50 is the best overall, a genuine 4K set with HDR10 and Fire TV at a mid-size price. The 85 inch version suits large rooms and basement theaters. For smaller spaces, the 32 inch Insignia F20 is the cheaper choice, the Amazon Ember is the house-brand alternative, and the 24 inch F20 fits desks and tiny kitchens.
intro: A Fire TV is a television with Amazon's streaming software built in, so the box or stick you would otherwise plug in is already inside. What remains for you to decide is hardware: screen size and resolution. Because the software is identical across these sets, the real choice is which room it goes in, and how far from the screen you sit.

Five models are ranked here, spanning 24 to 85 inches. Streaming sticks are left out on purpose, since this guide is about the television itself. Our editors reviewed the listings and scored each set on the Primea framework, weighing resolution, size for the room, remote, price tier and how well each panel suits its intended use. Sound and mounting are judged from the listing, not assumed.

products.name: INSIGNIA 50" Class F50 Series 4K Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: A genuine 4K panel with HDR10, plus Fire TV and Alexa built in, at a mid-size price.
products.description:
The 50 inch F50 puts a 4K panel, HDR10 and the Fire TV system into the screen size where 4K begins to pay off. HDR10 widens the gap between bright and dark areas on supported content, and the Alexa Voice Remote saves a separate stick. From about 6 to 10 feet, the extra resolution is visible.

It wins because 50 inches is the point at which 4K shows its worth, and the built-in software removes a streaming box. It costs more than the 32 inch sets, but it is the best balance of price and picture in the group.

Buy it for a living room or den. The caveats are the speakers, which are thin, as on most slim sets, and size: it is too big for a small bedroom. Plan on a soundbar if you care about dialogue.
pros: Fire TV and Alexa built in

products.name: INSIGNIA 85" Class F50 Series 4K Smart Fire TV with Alexa
products.verdict: The same 4K, HDR10 and Fire TV package, stretched to 85 inches for a home theater wall.
products.description:
The 85 inch F50 shares the 50 inch set's platform: 4K UHD, HDR10 and Fire TV with Alexa built in. At 85 inches, it is the largest screen in the ranking, and at $500 and up it is also the most expensive. A screen this size turns a spare wall into a small cinema.

It ranks second because few rooms suit it. At 85 inches you want to sit 9 to 14 feet back, and the set needs a sturdy stand or a mount rated well above its weight. For a basement theater or a large living room it is the best value here.

Buy it for a big room with enough viewing distance. Skip it if your seating is under 8 feet from the wall, because the picture will overwhelm the space.
pros: Fire TV and Alexa built in
products.idealFor: Basement theaters and large living rooms.
products.skipIf: Your seating is under 8 feet away.

products.name: INSIGNIA 32" Class F20 Series Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: Fire TV, an Alexa Voice Remote and the lowest price among the 32-inch sets.
products.description:
The 32 inch F20 is an HD Fire TV with an Alexa Voice Remote, and it is the least expensive 32 inch set in this ranking, in the $50 to $100 bucket. For a bedroom, dorm or kitchen, HD at this size looks sharp from a normal viewing distance.

It ranks third because it lacks the 4K and HDR10 of the larger sets, and the speakers are basic. Against the Ember, it is the cheaper choice for the same screen size and platform.

Buy it for a second room where the television runs a few hours a day, or for a guest room. The caveat: HD only means it will not age well if you later move it to a living room. A soundbar is the first upgrade.
pros: Good for a kitchen or dorm

products.name: Amazon Ember 32" 2-Series with Fire TV
products.verdict: Amazon's house-brand 32-inch set, running Fire TV out of the box.
products.description:
The Ember 2-Series is a 32 inch TV that Amazon makes itself, running Fire TV natively. Because Amazon builds both the hardware and the software, the interface and updates are consistent, and Alexa integration is tight.

It ranks fourth because it is close in spec to the Insignia 32 inch and costs more, in the $100 to $200 bucket. What the difference buys is Amazon's own branding and a more direct support path if something fails.

Buy it if you want the Amazon-made option for a small room. The caveat is value: it is HD only, with a plain panel, and the Insignia delivers the same screen size, resolution and platform for less. Unless the brand matters, the Insignia is the smarter purchase.
products.idealFor: Amazon households with a small room.

products.name: INSIGNIA 24" Class F20 Series Smart Fire TV
products.verdict: The smallest Fire TV here, for desks, shelves and tiny rooms.
products.description:
The 24 inch F20 is the smallest Fire TV in the ranking, an HD set with an Alexa Voice Remote and the same software as the bigger models. It fits on a desk, a shelf or a small kitchen counter, and it sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It ranks last because 24 inches is too small for a main viewing room. It is the right choice when space is the limit, such as a dorm desk, a workshop or an RV.

Buy it for a spot where nothing larger fits and one person watches from close range. The caveat: it is not suitable for group viewing, and the built-in speakers are small. Sit within about three feet, or add a small speaker, to hear dialogue clearly.
products.skipIf: You watch from across a room.

whatMatters.factor: Fire TV is built in, not bolted on
whatMatters.detail: A Fire TV television runs Amazon's software natively, so there is no stick to plug in. You still pay for streaming services separately, and the home screen shows recommendations and ads. If that bothers you, consider whether the same panel is sold with a different interface. Check the listing title for the words Fire TV, and confirm it is the television rather than a stick.

At 32 inches viewed from a few feet, 4K looks almost the same as HD. From 50 inches and above, the extra detail becomes visible. Pay for 4K only if your screen size and seating distance justify it. Check the resolution line, which here separates the 50 and 85 inch sets from the HD models.

HDR10 widens the range between bright and dark parts of a picture on content that supports it. Entry-level sets cannot match premium HDR, but they still look livelier than non-HDR panels. Look for HDR10 in the listing, and note that only the 50 and 85 inch sets here state it. Treat it as a bonus, not a premium feature.

Large sets need a stand at least as wide as the feet, and an 85 inch panel is heavy. Check the mounting pattern and weight on the listing, and use a mount rated above the television's weight. A wall mount needs studs, not just drywall. Measure the furniture before ordering, not after, and leave a few inches behind the set for cables.

whatMatters.factor: Sound is usually the weak spot
whatMatters.detail: Thin televisions have small speakers, and dialogue is usually the first thing to suffer. If you care about voices and bass, plan on a soundbar. Check that the television has an HDMI ARC port or optical output so you can connect one. Look in the listing ports section rather than assuming, because budget sets sometimes skip optical.

faq.q: Do Fire TVs need a separate streaming stick?
faq.a: No. A Fire TV television has the software built in. You only need a stick for a television without a smart system, which is why none are ranked here.

faq.q: Do I need an Amazon account?
faq.a: You sign in with an Amazon account to set up the television, though you do not need Prime. Streaming services are billed separately, so budget for the apps you plan to use. Free ad-supported services are available.

faq.q: Is 4K worth it on a Fire TV?
faq.a: At 50 inches and above, yes. At 32 inches or smaller, HD is plenty. The Insignia 50 inch and 85 inch are the 4K models here, and the 24 and 32 inch sets are HD, which is perfectly adequate at those sizes.

faq.q: Can I control other devices with the remote?
faq.a: The Alexa Voice Remote can control compatible smart-home devices and the television itself. Check the listing for supported features on each model, since not every set includes every function, and voice features can change with software updates.

faq.q: What size Fire TV should I buy?
faq.a: Match the diagonal to the distance, roughly 1.5 to 2.5 times the screen size in viewing distance. A 50 inch set suits 6 to 10 feet, and a 32 inch set suits 4 to 6 feet.

faq.q: Does a Fire TV show ads?
faq.a: The home screen includes recommendations and sponsored content. You can reduce some of it in settings, but not remove it entirely. Consider this before you buy, especially for a bedroom set. Weigh this before you buy if you dislike promotions.

finalTake: Buy the Insignia 50 inch for a main living room, or the 85 inch if you have the wall and the seating distance. Choose the F20 32 inch for a bedroom, dorm or kitchen, and the 24 inch for a desk. Pay for the Ember only if you prefer Amazon-made hardware.
